chunks.content: Care Home — Diabetes & Insulin Safe-Practice (summary policy) Purpose Ensure safe, person-centred care for residents with diabetes, including safe insulin use, blood-glucose monitoring, hypoglycaemia/hyperglycaemia management, medicines storage and sharps handling. Scope All staff (nurses, care workers, domiciliary staff, managers) involved in care, medicines or food provision for residents with diagnosed or suspected diabetes. Key principles Person-centred care plans for every resident with diabetes, reviewed regularly and after any change in condition. Only trained, competent staff may administer insulin or perform delegated clinical tasks. Delegation must follow local RN supervision and documented competency checks. Residents should be supported to self-manage wherever safe and agreed in care plan. Roles & responsibilities Registered nurse (RN): overall clinical accountability for delegation, initial competency assessment, periodic re-competency checks, review insulin regimens with prescribers.

Roles & responsibilities Registered nurse (RN): overall clinical accountability for delegation, initial competency assessment, periodic re-competency checks, review insulin regimens with prescribers. Care worker / support staff: may accept delegated tasks only after accredited training/assessment; must follow care plan and escalate concerns. Manager: ensure policies, training, fridge/sharps provision, safe staffing and record audits. GP/Diabetes specialist team: prescribe, review treatment, provide specialist training/support. Assessment & care planning

On admission screen for diabetes risk and symptoms; document diagnosis and HbA1c, insulin regimen, monitoring schedule, hypo/ hyper triggers, dietary needs, swallowing/PEG info. Produce a diabetes passport/care plan with: responsible person, injection technique & times, target glucose ranges, sick-day rules, contact details for GP/DSN, consent and capacity notes. Training & competency Mandatory induction + annual update for staff who handle medicines or support diabetes care. Specific competency-based training for: blood glucose testing, insulin administration (pens/vials), mixed insulin technique, pen priming, rotation of sites, handling hypo, flash/CGM support (if used), and sharps safety. Maintain signed competency records and RN assessment of delegation. Insulin administration & devices Use only the prescribed insulin, device and needle size. Check resident ID, insulin name, dose, expiry and that pen is primed. Never withdraw insulin from a pre-filled pen with a syringe.

Check resident ID, insulin name, dose, expiry and that pen is primed. Never withdraw insulin from a pre-filled pen with a syringe. Rotate injection sites and record site used to avoid lipohypertrophy. Palpate injection sites as part of routine checks. Blood-glucose monitoring & CGM Define who monitors and when (e.g., before meals, bedtime, on illness). Targets agreed in care plan (individualised). Staff must be trained on the specific meter, quality-control, calibration and recording. Keep meter QC records and strip expiry checks. For CGM/flash: support scanning as per manufacturer and diabetes team guidance; capillary checks remain the backup. Hypoglycaemia management

Hypo threshold and immediate treatment plan in each care plan (e.g., fast-acting carbohydrate: 15–20g oral unless unconscious; GlucoGel/juice; if unconscious — call 999 and follow emergency protocol; emergency glucagon where indicated). Keep standard hypo kits (contents list) accessible and recorded. Document all episodes and inform GP/diabetes team. Hyperglycaemia / DKA awareness Signs to watch (polyuria, polydipsia, vomiting, abdominal pain, Kussmaul breathing, confusion). If suspected, test ketones and escalate per care plan — urgent medical review/admission if DKA suspected. Medicines storage & fridges Store insulin and fridge-required meds at 2–8°C in a dedicated medicines fridge. Record min/max/current temperatures daily with min/max thermometer; keep action logs for excursions. Do not store food. Follow manufacturer guidance for opened pens (room temp limited period). Sharps & waste Provide appropriate sharps bins; never recap needles (unless specific assessed procedure and one-handed recapping device).

Sharps & waste Provide appropriate sharps bins; never recap needles (unless specific assessed procedure and one-handed recapping device). Arrange safe collection/disposal. Include arrangements for residents who self-inject at home (local authority collection or contractor). Infection control & disposal Single-use needles; dispose after use. Safe hand hygiene before/after procedures. Routine cleaning and maintenance of equipment. Documentation & records Record each insulin dose given, blood glucose readings, injection site, any refusals, hypoglycaemic/hyperglycaemic events, and following actions. Keep delegation agreements and competency files.

Consent & capacity Assess capacity for diabetes self-management. If lacking capacity, follow best interest processes and involve family/advocate/GPA as appropriate. Document decisions and who was consulted. Sick-day rules / acute illness Have written sick-day guidance covering fluid intake, when to check ketones, when to contact GP/diabetes team, and when to seek emergency care. Audit & quality assurance Annual diabetes care audit (medicines management, fridge temps, hypoglycaemic events, staff competency, care plans). Action plan and re-audit within 1 month for gaps. Links & escalation Provide contact list for GP, out-of-hours service, diabetes specialist nurse, local pharmacy, and emergency services. Ensure staff know out-of-hours procedures. Appendices / templates to include Diabetes passport / care-plan template. Insulin administration competency checklist (RN sign off). Blood glucose chart / record sheet. Hypo box contents list + flowchart for treatment. Fridge temp log & excursion action template.

Insulin administration competency checklist (RN sign off). Blood glucose chart / record sheet. Hypo box contents list + flowchart for treatment. Fridge temp log & excursion action template. Sharps disposal process and collection schedule. Audit checklist. Consent & capacity checklist for medicines administration. Sick-day rules (type 1 and type 2).
Staff training syllabus and training log.
